title: BCG Moreau Vaccine Safety Profile and NK Cells-Double Protection Against Disseminated BCG Infection in Retrospective Study of BCG Vaccination in 52 Polish Children with Severe Combined Immunodeficiency.
ehr_evidence: The profiles of 52 SCID patients vaccinated at birth with BCG, hospitalized in Children's Memorial Health Institute, Warsaw (CMHI), in the years 1980–2015 were compared with those of 349 BCG-vaccinated SCID patients from other countries analyzed by Beatriz E. Marciano et al.
summary: A retrospective single-center study of 52 Polish SCID patients vaccinated at birth with the BCG Moreau vaccine at CMHI Warsaw (1980–2015) comparing rates of disseminated BCG infection and immunological predictors (NK cells) with a multicenter retrospective study of 349 SCID patients.
key_findings: Disseminated BCG infection occurred in 10 of 52 (19%) CMHI patients versus 119 of 349 (34%) in the Marciano study (p = 0.0028).
The absolute number of NK cells was significantly lower (p = 0.0161) and B cells significantly higher (p = 0.0126) in the CMHI group with BCG complications.
Disseminated BCG complications occurred only in 18 of 52 SCID patients with low NK cell counts (p < 0.000001).
The number of T cells did not significantly influence disseminated BCG (p = 0.0915).
Localized BCG complication rate was higher but not significantly (12 of 52, 24% vs 60 of 349, 17%; p = 0.2417).
Mortality was not significantly different (46 of 349, 13% vs 3 of 52, 5%; p = 0.1724).
HSCT was performed significantly more often in the CMHI cohort (43 of 52, 83%) than in the Marciano study (190 of 349, 54%; p = 0.0001).
captured_features: Genetic mutations (IL2RG, JAK3, RAG1/2, IL7RA, Artemis, MHC II, ZAP-70, Cernunnos)
Age at first symptoms and at diagnosis
Clinical manifestations (meningitis, bronchopneumonia, skin infection, osteomyelitis, liver/spleen abscess)
study_design: Retrospective single-center cohort compared with a multicenter retrospective study
population: 52 Caucasian Polish children with SCID, born in Central-Eastern Poland and vaccinated at birth with BCG Moreau vaccine, hospitalized at the Department of Immunology, CMHI Warsaw (1980–2015); mean age at first symptoms 3.3 months, mean age at diagnosis 13.5 months.
limitations: Retrospective design with long time span (1980–2015) and changing clinical practices.
Comparison with a different multicenter study (Marciano et al.) with differing cohort characteristics and vaccine policies.
